timeline.title: The revision is ordered, starting with Bihar
timeline.text: The Election Commission ordered a Special Intensive Revision "in the entire country", starting with Bihar, with the schedule for the rest of the country to follow. Only electors whose enumeration forms came back would be on the draft roll. The 2003 Bihar roll, from the state's last intensive revision, was treated as evidence of eligibility, including a presumption of citizenship. Anyone not on it had to give documents from an indicative list of 11, and the younger the elector, the more were needed. Those born before 1 July 1987 gave their own. Those born up to 2 December 2004 gave their own and one parent's, and those born later gave their own and both parents'. A new declaration had to go with every Form 6 for a new voter, and with Form 8 for anyone moving into Bihar. No name could be deleted from the draft without an inquiry. Appeals lay to the District Magistrate and then the Chief Electoral Officer, the Commission's officer in charge of the roll in each state.

timeline.title: Bihar's schedule
timeline.text: Enumeration, the round of forms, was set for 25 June to 26 July 2025. The draft roll was due on 1 August, claims and objections were open from 1 August to 1 September, and the final roll was due on 30 September 2025. Forms received before 25 July would go into the draft.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

timeline.title: The 2003 roll goes online
timeline.text: The 2003 Bihar roll, with 4.96 crore electors, was put online. Anyone on it needed no documents. Anyone not on it could use a parent's entry in it in place of documents for that parent.

src.name: CEO Bihar, press notes on the SIR, 2025

timeline.title: The Supreme Court hears the challenge
timeline.text: The Court issued notice on the petitions against the 24 June order. It observed that the Commission should also consider Aadhaar, the voter identity card and the ration card, but gave no direction to accept them. This account of the hearing comes from the Court's judgment of 27 May 2026.

timeline.title: Bihar's draft roll
timeline.text: The draft roll was published, and claims and objections were open until 1 September. No name was to be deleted from the draft without a hearing and a written order.

timeline.title: The names left off must be published
timeline.text: The Court recorded the Commission's agreement to publish the roughly 65 lakh names left off the draft with the reason for each. The lists were to go up district by district, searchable by EPIC number (the number on the voter identity card), online and on panchayat and block notice boards. The public notice was to say that a claim could be made with a copy of Aadhaar.

timeline.title: Political parties brought in
timeline.text: Twelve political parties were made parties to the case. They were told to have their booth agents help voters file forms with any of the 11 documents or with Aadhaar. This account of the order comes from the 2026 judgment.

timeline.title: Claims after the deadline
timeline.text: The Commission told the Court that claims, objections and corrections could still be made after 1 September and would be considered up to the last date of nominations. The Court directed the chairman of the Bihar State Legal Services Authority to have the district legal services authorities send para-legal volunteers to help voters and parties file them online. This account of the order also comes from the 2026 judgment.

timeline.title: Aadhaar becomes the 12th document
timeline.text: The Court directed that Aadhaar be accepted as the 12th document, as proof of identity. The Court said it is no proof of citizenship, and the authorities remained free to verify each card.

timeline.title: The Commission follows the order
timeline.text: The Commission told the Chief Electoral Officer of Bihar that Aadhaar is the 12th document, as proof of identity, and that it is no proof of citizenship.

src.name: ECI letter of 09.09.2025 to CEO Bihar

timeline.title: Bihar's final roll
timeline.text: The final roll was published with about 7.42 crore electors. Appeals lay to the District Magistrate and then the Chief Electoral Officer.

timeline.title: Twelve more states and union territories
timeline.text: The revision was extended to Andaman and Nicobar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Puducherry, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal, on the June order with changes. No documents were to be collected while forms were filled in. The form asked instead for the elector's own entry, or a relative's, in the state's last intensive revision, and after the draft notices would go only to those who could not be linked to it. For every form not returned, the booth-level officer (BLO), the official who looks after the roll for one polling booth, was to record a probable reason (absent, shifted, dead or duplicate). The declaration with Form 6 was changed, and BLOs were to carry at least 30 blank copies of Form 6 with it.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

timeline.title: Which old roll counts
timeline.text: Each state's forms are linked to the roll of its last intensive revision, and the Commission fixed which year that was. Linking an elector to that old roll is called mapping. West Bengal, Kerala, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Goa go back to 2002. Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Bihar go back to 2003. Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh go back to 2005, and Arunachal Pradesh to 2006. Tamil Nadu has two, 2002 for 197 seats and 2005 for 37.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

timeline.title: The first Phase II schedule
timeline.text: Enumeration was set for 4 November to 4 December 2025 and the draft for 9 December. Claims ran to 8 January 2026, notices to 31 January, and the final roll was due on 7 February 2026.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

timeline.title: Assam gets a different revision
timeline.text: Assam was given a "Special Revision" in place of an intensive one. Booth officers were to check house to house from 22 November to 20 December 2025, with a register already filled in for them. The draft was due on 27 December, claims ran to 22 January 2026, and the final roll was due on 10 February 2026. The pages read give no reason for the difference.

src.name: ECI letter of 17.11.2025 to CEO Assam (instructions listing, eci.gov.in)

timeline.title: Anta gets its own dates
timeline.text: Rajasthan's Anta seat could not follow the 27 October schedule because a bye-election was under way, so it was given its own. Enumeration started on 8 December 2025, the draft was due on 12 January 2026, claims ran to 11 February and the final roll was due on 12 March 2026.

src.name: ECI letter of 27.11.2025 for 193-Anta, CEO Rajasthan

timeline.title: Every Phase II date moves a week
timeline.text: All twelve states and union territories got one more week. Enumeration now ran to 11 December, the draft was due on 16 December, claims ran to 15 January 2026, notices to 7 February, and the final roll was due on 14 February 2026.

src.name: ECI order of 30.11.2025, as published by CEO Goa

timeline.title: Lists before the draft
timeline.text: Before the draft, Chief Electoral Officers were to give party booth agents the booth-wise lists of those absent, shifted, dead or duplicated. After it, they were to put the lists online, searchable by EPIC number.

timeline.title: Seven move again
timeline.text: At the request of their Chief Electoral Officers the dates moved again. Tamil Nadu and Gujarat got drafts on 19 December, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Andaman and Nicobar on 23 December, and Uttar Pradesh on 31 December. Kerala had already been moved to a draft on 23 December. The same release also lists Gujarat among the states keeping the 16 December draft, and does not name Puducherry.

timeline.title: The "logical discrepancy" list
timeline.text: The Court said names in the "logical discrepancy" category, flagged because something in their link to the old roll did not match, may be displayed at panchayat, block and ward offices. Documents could be filed through an authorised representative such as a booth agent, the Commission was to allow ten more days from the display, and the Madhyamik admit card may be accepted.

timeline.title: More officers to help
timeline.text: The Court had 8,505 state officers report to the district and registration officers to assist them, with the final decision left to the registration officers. Scrutiny was given at least a week beyond 14 February.

timeline.title: Judges decide the claims
timeline.text: Using its powers under Article 142, and with the parties' consent, the Court gave the deciding of claims and objections about inclusion to judicial officers of West Bengal, acting "for and on behalf of this Court". This account of the order comes from the Court's orders of 2 and 13 April 2026.

timeline.title: Judges from Jharkhand and Odisha, and no appeal to officials
timeline.text: A further order set out the work given to the judicial officers and said their orders could not be appealed before any executive or administrative officer. Judicial officers from Odisha and Jharkhand joined those of West Bengal, and by 10 March there were 200 of them beside more than 500 from West Bengal. This account of the order comes from the Court's order of 10 March 2026.

timeline.title: West Bengal's final roll, with 60 lakh held back
timeline.text: The final roll was published with 60,06,675 names marked "under adjudication". They were to be added by a supplementary list if the judicial officers approved them.

src.name: CEO West Bengal, press note CEO/PN-05/2026

timeline.title: Appeals go to tribunals
timeline.text: No executive officer could hear an appeal against an order of the judicial officers. Appeals were to go to tribunals of former Chief Justices and judges, which the Commission would notify in consultation with the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court.

timeline.title: Nineteen tribunals
timeline.text: Nineteen appellate tribunals were at work. Appeals decided by 21 and 27 April were to take effect through a supplementary roll before polling, and a pending appeal gave no right to vote.

timeline.title: The rest of the country
timeline.text: The revision was ordered in 16 states and 3 union territories, covering the whole country except Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, whose dates would be announced later. Eight separate schedules were set. After the draft, notices would go to those who could not be linked to the last intensive revision (the no-mapping list) and to those whose link showed a discrepancy. Lists of those sent notices were to be published.

src.name: Copy of the ECI order of 14.05.2026 (district site)

timeline.title: The Supreme Court upholds the revision
timeline.text: The Court disposed of the petitions. It held that the revision has its legal basis in section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act read with Article 324, that it was proportionate, and that its document list, with Aadhaar added, was not arbitrary. The Commission may enquire into citizenship only for electoral purposes and must refer doubtful cases to the competent authority of the Central Government. People domiciled in Bihar whose names were wrongly deleted as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate may seek judicial review.

timeline.title: Mizoram avoids Sundays
timeline.text: At its Chief Electoral Officer's request, Mizoram's draft moved from Sunday 5 July to 4 July 2026, and its final roll from Sunday 6 September to 7 September.

timeline.title: Karnataka three weeks later
timeline.text: Karnataka's draft came out on 24 August 2026 instead of 5 August. Enumeration ran to 17 August, claims to 23 September, and the final roll is due on 27 October instead of 7 October.

timeline.title: Maharashtra four weeks later
timeline.text: Maharashtra's draft came out on 31 August 2026 instead of 5 August. Claims run to 30 September, and the final roll is due on 4 November instead of 7 October.

timeline.title: Documents at the door, and a drive for those left off
timeline.text: For people sent notices as unmapped or for logical discrepancies, BLOs would collect documents at home and upload them for the registration officer, so these people need not come to the office. A hearing would be held only in exceptional cases, as the registration officer decides, preferably online, and a family member authorised by the elector could attend. The Commission said the declaration attached to Form 6 for the revision had been upheld by the Supreme Court, and that outside the revision the forms in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 apply. Claims were extended in Delhi to 30 October and in Maharashtra to 12 October 2026. Where the revision was complete, in 20 states and union territories, anyone left out during it or after, and any young or first-time voter, could ask the registration officer to be added under continuous updation, and the Chief Electoral Officers, district officers and registration officers were to launch a special drive at once to enrol them.

timeline.title: Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya extended
timeline.text: Andhra Pradesh's notices run to 10 October and its final roll is due on 16 October 2026. Meghalaya's final roll moves to 26 October 2026.

timeline.title: The drive after the revision, in writing
timeline.text: The Commission wrote to every Chief Electoral Officer setting out a special drive to enrol electors left off and young or first-time voters. Booth officers are to compare the current roll with the roll from before the revision, list everyone who was on the first and is missing from the second, visit them at home and help those found eligible fill in Form 6. The Commission asked them to cover at least 20 to 25 electors a week, so the work ends in about a month. The lists go to the booth agents of the recognised parties and then to the registration officer, who decides each case under the 1950 Act and the 1960 Rules. Booth camps are to be held, and special camps for people in night shelters, labour colonies and the homeless. The letter says anyone not on the roll, or whose name was deleted, can apply to be enrolled at any time.

src.name: ECI letter No. 23/2025/ERS(Vol-II) of 01.10.2026 to all Chief Electoral Officers

timeline.title: A drive to find the names left off
timeline.text: When it published Uttarakhand's final roll, the state's Chief Electoral Officer set out the Commission's directions for what follows. Booth officers are to compare the roll from before the revision with the current one and list the electors who were on the first and are missing from the second. They are to visit them at home and help those still eligible fill in Form 6. The lists are to be shared with the booth agents of the recognised parties, and booth and special camps held, including for people in night shelters, labour colonies and the homeless.

reported.headline: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps
reported.text: The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi formally objected on record at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders that, they say, were taken without their knowledge. It reported that the objections concerned new voter registration, deletion and restoration of voters, appeals against orders restoring voters, and the custody and security of the electoral roll, and said it had seen each of these exchanges.
reported.response: The Indian Express said the Commission and both Commissioners did not respond. The Hindu reported that the Commission said through sources that all its decisions, the revision included, had been unanimous, and then said in a written statement that written notes and internal checks are standard practice and that all its actions were lawful.

reported.headline: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps
reported.text: In the same report, The Indian Express reported that in August Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu wrote to Commission officials asking who had authorised and who had filed appeals on behalf of the Commission against voters whom judicial officers had included in West Bengal. It reported that he recorded that neither he, nor Commissioner Vivek Joshi, nor the current Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal had been informed of the basis or process of filing those appeals.
reported.response: The Indian Express said the Commission and both Commissioners did not respond. The Commission's statement on the series is under the entry above.

reported.headline: Disquiet within, all three Election Commissioners meet, take first steps
reported.text: The Indian Express reported that after the full Commission met on 26 September it announced nine decisions that matched, almost item for item, the concerns the two Commissioners had put on file. Agendas would be circulated before every meeting and minutes issued after it, officers’ foreign trips would need the Commission’s approval, new IT modules would go through a committee of officers, ECINet would be reviewed by a committee with an independent expert from an IIT or IIIT, and field officers would be given any further flexibility they needed in the software.
reported.response: The paper reported that the decisions did not say who added the declaration to the online Form 6 in July, who authorised the appeals filed in West Bengal against electors that judicial officers had included, or why Goa’s request to reverse its officers’ decisions was never met.

reported.headline: Express Special | EC changes Form 6 for new voters without amendment to rules; seeks SIR details of parents
reported.text: The Indian Express reported that the online Form 6 on the Commission's ECINET portal carried a new declaration asking whether the applicant or their parents or grandparents were in the electoral roll of the last SIR, although the statutory form had not been amended. It reported that although the section was not marked mandatory, applicants could not submit the form without completing it, and that the downloadable Form 6 on the same portal did not include it.
reported.response: The EC did not respond to a request for comment and Legislative Department Secretary Rajiv Mani could not be reached despite repeated attempts.

reported.headline: ‘Illegal, unauthorised’: Election Commissioners objected to Form 6 change
reported.text: The Indian Express reported, from internal records it investigated, that on May 16 Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi recorded that Form 6 is prescribed by statute and cannot be altered without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and that Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu concurred on May 19. It reported that the declaration was added to the online form anyway, and that on August 13 Sandhu wrote that the changes were unauthorised and illegal and must be removed immediately.

reported.headline: EC removes Form 6 change two Commissioners had called ‘illegal’
reported.text: The Indian Express reported that on the night of 29 to 30 September 2026 the Commission removed the SIR declaration from the online Form 6 on ECINET for states where the final SIR rolls have been published. It reported that the declaration remained for states where the SIR is still ongoing.
reported.response: The article cites the Commission's September 26 announcement that ‘for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used’.

reported.headline: Form-7 misuse: Supreme Court to consider Congress MP’s plea alleging targeted deletions in U.P.
reported.text: The Hindu reported that the Supreme Court agreed to consider an application by Congress MP Tanuj Punia alleging that Form 7 objections in the Uttar Pradesh SIR were filed with false particulars, forged signatures and in the names of people who later denied filing them. The application cited one person filing objections against 32 electors in Hata, Kushinagar, and a UP Congress claim of 700 to 800 objections in four Khalilabad booths.

reported.headline: Uttarakhand SIR: Who is targeting Muslim voters?
reported.text: Newslaundry reported from its investigation in Uttarakhand that numerous applications were filed to remove Muslim voters from the rolls, many in the names of people it said were associated with the BJP. It reported that some people named as objectors later filed affidavits saying they had never filed the objections and that their names, EPIC numbers and signatures had been used fraudulently.

reported.headline: Civil society groups, Congress demand FIRs over bulk Form 7s seeking deletion of names
reported.text: The Hindu reported that as of September 28, 4,000 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names had been filed in Karnataka, which it said mostly targeted Muslim voters. It reported that ten people filed Form 7s seeking deletion of 1,363 names in Babaleshwar in one day, often on forms with the voters' details already printed and only the objector's name handwritten. Civil society groups and the Karnataka Congress demanded that the Commission lodge criminal complaints.
reported.response: V. Anbukumar, CEO, Karnataka, was not available for comment.

reported.headline: Karnataka SIR: ECI flags bulk Form 7 claims, orders action against false declarations
reported.text: The New Indian Express reported that the Commission wrote to election officials in Bengaluru that bulk Form 7 applications had come to its notice, with allegations that some were not authentic. It reported that the Commission directed Electoral Registration Officers to act against applicants who knowingly make false declarations, after an inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

reported.headline: Karnataka: 43.43 lakh SIR notices delivered, 84,900 Form 7 applications received so far
reported.text: Vartha Bharati reported, quoting the Chief Electoral Officer's office, that Karnataka received 8,85,952 Form 6, 4,648 Form 6A, 84,900 Form 7 and 11,78,028 Form 8 applications between 16 June and 1 October, and that 35,60,833 hearings had been held, with 7,82,304 pending.
reported.response: The figures are a running count while hearings continue. Karnataka's final roll is due on 27 October 2026.

reported.headline: How ECI’s dubious software branded 3.66 crore voters in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh as suspects
reported.text: The Reporters' Collective reported, from internal Commission records it acquired, that the Commission's software initially flagged 1.31 crore voters in West Bengal and 2.35 crore in Madhya Pradesh for logical discrepancies, and that officials had no written instructions on how to resolve them. It reported that no criteria for deciding which flagged voters to summon had been made public.
reported.response: The Collective said the Commission did not answer its question on how flagged voters were chosen, and that questions sent to the Commission and three state offices on testing and procedure went unanswered.

reported.headline: ECI misled the Supreme Court on SIR in West Bengal
reported.text: The Reporters' Collective reported that hearing notices in West Bengal were generated in bulk by the Commission's software for logical discrepancies, and that two EROs it spoke to, with a few deputies, were signing 4,000 to 5,000 printed notices each day. It reported that the software transliterated names from Bengali into English before matching, so that spellings such as Xalxo and Khalkho triggered a discrepancy. The Collective said this showed the Commission had misled the Supreme Court, where it said there was no automated generation of notices.
reported.response: The Collective said the Commission had not responded by publication. It set its finding against the Commission's submission to the Court that "There is no automated generation of notices" and that officers were "signing them off after application of mind".

reported.headline: The many categories of SIR’s logical discrepancy list keep voters on toes
reported.text: The Hindu reported that up to 11 categories of logical discrepancy were being applied in the third phase of the SIR, up from four when the concept was introduced in West Bengal. They include a sibling age gap of nine months or less, which flagged a Delhi resident's twin children, and a marital mapping mismatch where a woman is linked to her father in the old roll and her husband in the new. It reported that the term has never been clearly defined in any official communication.

reported.headline: SIR: Not even 0.5% submit enumeration forms online amid website glitches
reported.text: The Hindu reported that 13 days into the Karnataka SIR only 0.41% of enumeration forms had been submitted online, and that voters complained of captcha failures, server errors and an ECINet search that failed to find records appearing in the published rolls. It reported that online submission required a current mobile number linked to the voter's EPIC.
reported.response: Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar said the process was still under way. However, the CEO did not comment on the technical glitches reported by voters.

reported.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity
reported.text: The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi warned on file, from November 2025 to August 2026, that control of the electoral roll software was being centralised in the Commission's IT division. It reported that on August 14 Sandhu wrote that many Chief Electoral Officers, District Election Officers and Electoral Registration Officers had told him they lacked proper and complete access to ERONet, and that on July 29 both Commissioners wrote separately to the Cabinet Secretary about a change in work allocation.
reported.response: The Election Commission and the two ECs, Sandhu and Joshi, did not respond to calls and questionnaires emailed by The Indian Express seeking comment.

reported.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out: EC’s flawed system
reported.text: The Indian Express reported that Goa's Electoral Registration Officers heard electors flagged for logical discrepancies and found 97 of them eligible, but could not reverse the earlier decisions on ECINET because the permission was controlled from Delhi. It reported that the Goa Chief Electoral Officer's office wrote eight times in seven days asking for a rollback option, and that all 97 were missing from the final roll published on February 21 and were still missing on September 20.
reported.response: Goa's Chief Electoral Officer, Sanjay Goel, told the paper the decision not to include them was the Commission's. The Indian Express later reported that the Commission said, after its meeting of 26 September, that 81 of the 97 had filled Form 6 and that the Chief Electoral Officer had been told to help include them.

reported.headline: How booth-level officers in Bihar are deleting voters arbitrarily
reported.text: Scroll reported that its analysis found 200 booths across 58 constituencies in 26 Bihar districts where between 324 and 641 names were deleted from the draft roll, 77,454 in all. It reported that most deleted voters its team met in 10 of those booths had been marked absent or shifted though they had lived at their addresses for years, and that interviews with 17 BLOs showed no consistent procedure for deciding deletions.
reported.response: Parth Gupta, electoral registration officer for Purnia, acknowledged that one deleted voter should not have been asked for her parents' documents, and said, “Please provide her details and I will look into it.” Scroll also reported that Election Commission spokespersons and Bihar Chief Electoral Officer Vinod Singh Gunjiyal did not respond to requests for comment.

reported.headline: ‘I didn’t know my name was deleted’: Voters in Okhla on the pre-SIR ‘clean-up’
reported.text: Newslaundry reported that several voters in Delhi's Okhla constituency whose names were removed before the SIR began said they got no notice or hearing and learnt of the deletion only when they tried to take part in the SIR. It reported that 34,644 names were deleted in Okhla during the 2026 mapping phase, against 9,170 in all of 2025.
reported.response: Delhi Chief Electoral Officer Ashok Kumar said that no voter had been deleted without an inquiry and an opportunity for a hearing.

reported.headline: Declared Dead in Draft Electoral Roll, Bihar Voter Appears in Supreme Court
reported.text: The Wire reported that a voter from Ara, Bhojpur, who had been declared dead in the Bihar draft roll, appeared alive in the Supreme Court on 12 August 2025, produced by petitioner Yogendra Yadav. The voter told The Wire he had filled the enumeration form and that the BLO came to his house only after he complained.
reported.response: Senior advocate Rakesh Dwivedi, for the Commission, called the production of the voter "drama". The bench of Justices Surya Kant and Joymalya Bagchi said there may have been an "inadvertent error", which could be rectified.

reported.topic: Errors and duplicates in the roll
reported.headline: New voters list in Indian state includes wrong photos and dead people
reported.text: The BBC reported that voters in villages near Patna told it the Bihar draft roll carried wrong photographs, duplicate entries and the name of a person who died more than five years earlier. It reported that in Danara village many residents were not sure officials had visited their homes.
reported.response: In response to the BBC's questions, the Election Commission shared its 24 June order on conducting the SIR and a 27 July press note outlining efforts to ensure no eligible voter was "left behind". "Further, [the commission] does not take any responsibility of any other misinformation or unsubstantiated allegations being floated around by some vested interests," it added. The BBC also noted the commission has said BLOs worked "very responsibly".

reported.topic: Errors and duplicates in the roll
reported.headline: ECI Skipped its Fraud-Busting Software, Flooding Bihar Voter Roll with Lakhs of Suspect Duplicates
reported.text: The Reporters' Collective reported that a top Commission official and four Bihar EROs confirmed to it that the Commission did not run its de-duplication software during the Bihar SIR and did not give state officials access to it. It quoted the official saying the focus was on document collection. It reported that its own earlier analysis of the final roll found 14.35 lakh suspect duplicate entries.
reported.response: The Collective said the Commission and Bihar's Chief Electoral Officer did not answer its emailed questions. In person, the Chief Electoral Officer told its reporter "We cannot share this information with you" and said the Supreme Court was hearing the matter.

reported.headline: Bihar booth officials accept voter forms without documents, using discretion
reported.text: India Today reported from Hajipur and Muzaffarpur that BLOs were accepting and submitting enumeration forms without supporting documents at their own discretion. It reported that BLOs admitted the practice varied by location, with some accepting Aadhaar and others not.

reported.headline: Married women facing the heat of SIR in Bihar
reported.text: The Hindu reported that married women in Bihar born after 1 July 1987 were struggling in the SIR because the documents they needed were in their parents' homes, and they lived in their marital homes. It quoted women in Araria and Katihar districts who said their parents had no documents to give, and a woman in Saharsa, born in 1965, whose parents had died and who did not know what documents she needed.

reported.headline: Pay loss, travel woes to reach SIR hearings; migrants forced to leave to ensure electoral enrollment
reported.text: The Telegraph reported that migrant workers from Samserganj in Murshidabad were served SIR hearing notices two to three days before their hearings and had to travel home from Uttar Pradesh and Kerala without reserved seats. One worker was summoned because his name appeared in the 2002 roll without a surname, and another arrived after the day's hearings had ended. It reported that, as of 1 January, the Commission had issued no directive allowing online hearings for those outside the state.
reported.response: Samserganj BDO Sujit Kumar Lodh said, “After receiving the notice, those who are unable to attend the hearing within the stipulated period because of being out of the house can submit a written application citing specific reasons, and a second hearing date will be scheduled for them later.”

reported.headline: A Centralised Batch System Challenged Bengal Voters Who Were Cleared by Judicial Officers, Records Show
reported.text: The Wire reported that tribunal orders in Murshidabad record the Additional Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal as the appellant against electors whom judicial officers had restored to the roll. It reported that appeal records it reviewed carry identical minute-level timestamps across different constituencies, including at least six appeals at 7.04 pm on 8 April 2026, which it reads as a sign that the appeals were filed by one script running centrally, and not one by one. It also reported a December 2025 letter from the WBCS (Executive) Officers' Association complaining of system-driven deletions that bypassed EROs.
reported.response: The Wire wrote that the Commission had not explained why it filed more than 16 lakh challenges, how the electors were chosen or what explains the batch pattern.

reported.headline: SIR summit: A 145-year climb for Bengal tribunal judge swamped with 5 lakh cases
reported.text: The Telegraph reported that Justice (retd) Indrajit Chatterjee, who presides over one of the 19 SIR appellate tribunals and hears appeals from 11 Murshidabad constituencies, has written to the Chief Justice of Calcutta High Court that he wants to resign, citing a long commute. He told the newspaper he can decide about 10 appeals a day and has decided 425, restoring 350, while around 5.3 lakh are pending before him. It also reported that two other tribunal judges had resigned earlier, citing personal reasons.
reported.response: An official of the state election commission said, “The tribunals were set up on the Supreme Court’s order. A panel headed by the chief justice of Calcutta High Court takes decisions regarding the functioning of the appellate tribunals. We cannot interfere.”

reported.headline: Two suicides, BLO protests threaten to disrupt SIR in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Rajasthan
reported.text: The Indian Express reported the deaths of two BLOs. The family of a BLO in Kannur, Kerala, alleged he was under pressure to finish by December 4, and police said a note found on a BLO in Jaipur said he faced extreme pressure from his supervisor and was told he would be suspended if he did not meet his SIR target. It also reported that revenue employees in Tamil Nadu announced a statewide boycott of SIR work over workload.
reported.response: Kannur District Collector Arun K Vijayan's report indicated that the BLO was not under any work pressure. The Indian Express said its multiple calls and messages to Rajasthan CEO Naveen got no response.

reported.headline: 4 deaths in a week: 2 woman assistant BLOs die of ‘heart attack’ in Gujarat amid concerns on ‘SIR work pressure’
reported.text: The Indian Express reported that two women assistant BLOs died of heart attacks in Tapi and Vadodara districts, bringing BLO deaths in Gujarat that week to four. The husband of one said she was a heart patient who had asked to be excused from BLO duty, which the Vadodara Collector disputed.
reported.response: Vadodara District Collector Anil Dhameliya said, “We checked with the institute as well as with the local officials. She had not made any official request to be excused (from BLO duty)… We have learnt now that she was suffering from a heart ailment and had episodes of fainting in her institute as well.” He also said, “We have been cautious about ensuring that there is no excessive workload on the BLOs and therefore, we have appointed additional staff to assist in the process.” An unnamed government official said, “With a large workforce of over two lakh involved in the SIR work, these deaths can be termed as natural. Linking these to SIR is not justified and logical.”

reported.headline: Little sleep, no pay: India's poll workers flag harsh conditions amid uproar over deaths
reported.text: The BBC reported that 10 BLOs it spoke to in Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal said they worked 14 to 15 hours a day with little rest, and that families linked the deaths of more than a dozen poll workers, by alleged suicide or heart attack, to election work stress. The BBC said it had not independently verified the causes of death. It reported BLOs saying the SIR app crashed often and that many had not been paid.
reported.response: The BBC said the Commission did not answer its questions. It cited media reports of a court affidavit in which the Commission called claims linking booth officers' deaths to the revision "false, exaggerated and politically motivated".

reported.headline: Elderly man dies due to cardiac arrest during SIR hearing, kin allege ‘excessive stress’
reported.text: The Indian Express reported that a 75-year-old man died of cardiac arrest, according to hospital sources, after falling ill in a queue for an SIR hearing at the Rampurhat-1 block office in Birbhum. His wife and family alleged the SIR process had caused him excessive stress and held the Election Commission responsible. It also reported that an elderly man died of cardiac arrest at an SIR hearing in Howrah the previous day.

reported.headline: FIR against ECI in West Bengal over alleged suicide of elderly man due to SIR 'anxiety'
reported.text: The New Indian Express, citing PTI, reported that police in Purulia registered an FIR on a complaint by the son of an 82-year-old man who died allegedly by suicide on 29 December hours before he was due at an SIR hearing. An officer was quoted as saying the case included charges of abetment of suicide and criminal conspiracy against Election Commission officials, with no official named. The family alleged he acted out of anxiety over the SIR.

reported.headline: Supreme Court says modified Form 6 not approved by it
reported.text: LiveLaw reported that, hearing a petition against decisions said to have been taken by the Chief Election Commissioner without the other two Commissioners, Chief Justice Surya Kant said, "Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When the record is produced, we would like to see who has modified." It reported that the bench issued notice and tagged the petition with a similar one. Business Standard reported that notice went to the Commission and the Centre and that the bench declined to suspend the Chief Election Commissioner.
reported.response: No written order of the hearing had been published by 5 October 2026. The Commission's release of 26 September had said the declaration attached to Form 6 for the revision had been upheld by the Supreme Court.

reported.headline: After 13 crore names dropped from draft rolls, EC orders ‘left out’ voter drive
reported.text: The Indian Express reported a letter of 29 September from the Commission’s Secretary ordering a special drive to enrol "left out and young/first time eligible electors" in the 20 states and union territories where the revision is complete, using the statutory Form 6, with the added declaration kept for the revision phase only. It reported that at a video conference with all Chief Electoral Officers, the states were told to compare the roll from before the revision with the one after, list those removed, visit them at home and help those left out fill in Form 6, with help from the parties’ booth agents.
reported.response: The letter of 29 September itself was not found. The Commission's letter of 1 October, which continues it, is in the timeline above. The Commission’s press note of 26 September, in the timeline above, had already ordered the drive, and Uttarakhand’s Chief Electoral Officer set out its steps in a press note of 3 October.

reported.headline: After 13 crore names dropped from draft rolls, EC orders ‘left out’ voter drive
reported.text: The Indian Express reported a note from Maharashtra’s Chief Electoral Officer to the officers handling Mumbai City and Mumbai Suburban telling them not to remove any elector in haste. Before a name comes off, the elector is to be given a chance to submit documents, a hearing is to be held and an order passed. Booth officers are to collect documents at the homes of electors sent notices, and special camps were set for 3, 4, 10 and 11 October.
reported.response: The paper quoted the note as saying "an eligible voter should not remain excluded from the electoral roll" and that the changes to ECINet and the booth officers’ app were still being made at the Commission.

reported.headline: Final verification for 46.63L flagged voters launched
reported.text: The Hans India reported that Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer announced a door-to-door re-check of 46,62,583 names before the final roll of 16 October. They are the 44,89,512 left off the draft and the 1,73,071 found ineligible after notices, and booth officers are to help anyone left off in error file Form 6.
reported.response: The paper quoted the Chief Electoral Officer, Vivek Yadav, as saying the drive will recheck the flagged cases, and that a name found deleted by mistake is to be restored through Form 6 after verification.

forms.title: A declaration goes with Form 6
forms.text: The Bihar order required a new declaration, Annexure D (a form attached to the order), with every Form 6 from a new elector, and with Form 8 from anyone moving into Bihar from another state. Registration officers were to collect it also for Form 6 applications already pending and for advance claims for 1 October 2025.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

forms.title: What the Bihar declaration asked
forms.text: The applicant declared being over 18, ordinarily resident and a citizen, and ticked one of three birth groups. Those born in India before 1 July 1987 needed a document for themselves. Those born between 1 July 1987 and 2 December 2004 needed one for themselves and one for a parent. Those born after 2 December 2004 needed documents for themselves and both parents, and a parent's passport and visa if a parent was not Indian. The documents came from an indicative list of eleven, and an extract of Bihar's 2003 roll was enough on its own. A false declaration was punishable under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

forms.title: Form 6 for those whose forms did not come back
forms.text: An elector whose enumeration form was not handed in on time could file Form 6 with the declaration during the period for claims and objections. The Commission repeated this after meeting the parties on 3 July 2025.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala
CEO Bihar, press notes on the SIR, 2025

forms.title: Party agents may file forms in bulk
forms.text: Booth level agents, the people recognised parties appoint for each booth, could hand in forms in bulk. They could give the booth officer up to 50 a day before the draft roll and 10 a day after it, with a list and an undertaking that they had checked each one themselves.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

forms.title: How objections were to be handled
forms.text: No entry could be deleted from the draft without an inquiry and a fair and reasonable chance for the person to be heard. Appeals lay to the District Magistrate and then the Chief Electoral Officer. Claims and objections were to be listed every working day on the notice board and the Chief Electoral Officer's website, and given to the parties every week. Deletions and corrections are barred from the tenth day after an election is announced, so a Form 7 that arrives after that is decided after the election.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala
ECI letter of 14.05.2026, as published by CEO Maharashtra

forms.title: Claims could carry Aadhaar
forms.text: As an interim measure, the Court recorded the Commission's agreement that the public notice would say people left off the draft could make a claim with a copy of their Aadhaar card.

forms.title: Who could object in Bihar
forms.text: Party agents could collect claims and objections from the public, and could file objections themselves with a declaration that they had checked the part of the roll concerned. A person who was not an elector of the constituency could also object, on oath under Rule 20(3)(b) of the 1960 Rules. Complaints made without the prescribed form or declaration were not counted.

forms.title: Bihar's claims and objections at the deadline
forms.text: By 10 am on the last day, electors had filed 36,475 claims to be included and 2,17,049 objections to names on the roll. The parties' agents had filed 25 claims and 119 objections. New electors aged 18 or over had sent 16,56,886 Form 6, counted separately from claims to put names back.

forms.title: Bihar's final roll
forms.text: The Commission put the electors added after the draft at 21.53 lakh, counted as Form 6, and those removed from the draft as ineligible at 3.66 lakh. It said anyone eligible could still apply until ten days before the last date for nominations.

forms.title: A new declaration for Phase II
forms.text: For Phase II the Commission applied a modified declaration, Annexure IV. It asks for the applicant's or a relative's entry in the roll of the last intensive revision and carries three declarations, with no birth groups on the form. Documents are asked for when the registration officer sends a notice because those details are missing or do not match, and the same three birth groups then decide whose documents are needed. The list of documents added Aadhaar as the twelfth and an extract of the 2025 Bihar roll as the thirteenth. Booth officers were to carry at least 30 blank copies of Form 6 with the declaration on their house visits.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

forms.title: A representative may file for those flagged
forms.text: For people flagged for logical discrepancies in West Bengal, the Court allowed documents and objections to be filed through an authorised representative, who could be a party's booth agent, and gave everyone ten more days from the display of the lists.

forms.title: Phase III keeps the declaration
forms.text: The Phase III letter applies the same Annexure IV with Form 6, and with Form 8 for anyone moving in from another state. Its list of documents has twelve items and drops the Bihar roll extract. A person may link to their own or a relative's entry in the last intensive revision of the state, which for a state already revised includes its 2025 or 2026 roll. The limit on party agents' forms is unchanged.

src.name: ECI letter of 14.05.2026, as published by CEO Maharashtra

forms.title: The judgment on the documents
forms.text: The judgment records that new voters had to file Form 6 with the Annexure D declaration. It holds that the Commission has a bounded power to set what documents a revision asks for, that any departure from the statutory scheme needs a rational link to its purpose, and that the documentation regime is not arbitrary. That holding does not name the declaration.

forms.title: Form 6 outside the revision
forms.text: The Commission said the declaration attached to Form 6 for the revision had been upheld by the Supreme Court, and that outside the revision the forms of the 1960 Rules would be used. The Form 6 and Form 7 that can be downloaded from the Commission's portal are the forms of the Rules, and Form 7 sets no limit on how many objections one person may file.

forms.title: A second look at rejected Form 6
forms.text: Haryana's Chief Electoral Officer directed that electors found ineligible at a hearing, or whose Form 6 was rejected, be examined again, and said no name would be deleted without due reason. By then Haryana had received 3,77,987 Form 6, 40,162 Form 7 and 2,14,693 Form 8, issued 44,91,691 notices and heard 40,56,716 of them. Its final roll is due on 6 November 2026.

claims_note: Some Chief Electoral Officers said how many forms they received. Goa received 24,949 claims and objections and added 12,166 names, Manipur received 96,985 and added 56,871, and Arunachal Pradesh received 18,598 and added 8,803. Goa also marked 35,780 electors ineligible once its unmapped and logical discrepancy cases were decided. Haryana, whose claims closed on 30 September 2026, had by then received 3,77,987 Form 6, 40,162 Form 7 and 2,14,693 Form 8. ETV Bharat reported, from the district figures held by Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer, that 6,24,054 forms had come in from 31 August to 4 October, 6,05,097 of them Form 6, 11,251 Form 7 and 7,706 Form 8.

claims_src.name: CEO Goa, final roll press note of 21.02.2026
CEO Manipur, final roll press note of 06.09.2026
CEO Arunachal Pradesh, press note of 22.09.2026
ETV Bharat, 6 October 2026, from the district figures of the CEO Maharashtra (press)

burdens.title: A fresh form from every elector
burdens.text: Only electors whose enumeration forms came back were put on the draft roll. The enumeration form was a fresh form each elector on the roll had to fill in and return. The draft roll was the roll published from those forms, open to claims to add names and objections to names on it before the final roll. A name on the roll for years was left off the draft if its form did not come back in time, and its owner then had to ask to be put back.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

burdens.title: Parents' documents, by year of birth
burdens.text: In Bihar the younger the elector, the more documents were needed. Anyone born after 2 December 2004 needed documents for themselves and for both parents, and a parent's passport and visa if a parent was not Indian.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

burdens.title: Aadhaar only on the Court's order
burdens.text: Aadhaar was not on the first list of eleven documents. Claims could carry it from mid-August 2025, as the Commission agreed before the Supreme Court. It became the twelfth document on the Court's order of 8 September 2025, as proof of identity.

burdens.title: The declaration changed twice
burdens.text: Form 6, the application to be added to the roll, carried a new declaration from June 2025, a different one from October 2025, and a shorter list of documents from May 2026. No Gazette notification could be found amending the forms of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 to match.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala
ECI letter of 14.05.2026, as published by CEO Maharashtra

burdens.title: Dates moved after they were set
burdens.text: All {p2_states} Phase II states and union territories had their dates moved by a week, and {p2_again} were moved again. In Phase III, the orders and notes read for this page show dates moved in {p3_moved} of {p3_states}. An elector working to one deadline could find it had changed.

burdens.title: Anyone could object to anyone
burdens.text: Form 7 is the form for objecting to a name on the roll. A person who was not an elector of the constituency could object to a name on oath, a party agent could file ten forms a day after the draft, and Form 7 sets no limit on how many one person may file. In Bihar, objections to names on the roll outnumbered claims to be included by about six to one at the deadline.

src.name: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

burdens.title: Notices for logical discrepancies
burdens.text: People flagged for logical discrepancies, where something in their link to the old roll did not match, were called to hearings. The Supreme Court had to order that a representative could file for them and that they get ten more days. Only from September 2026 would booth officers collect their documents at home.

burdens.title: Sixty lakh held back in West Bengal
burdens.text: West Bengal's final roll left out 60,06,675 names marked under adjudication. They waited on judicial officers and then on nineteen tribunals, and a pending appeal gave no right to vote.

src.name: CEO West Bengal, press note CEO/PN-05/2026

burdens.title: Names added after the draft
burdens.text: {claims_lead} added fewer names after the draft, new electors included, than they removed at it, and {claims_under10} added fewer than 10 for every 100 removed.

events.title: No one else may do an ERO’s work
events.text: Acting on Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu’s directions, Deputy Election Commissioner Sanjay Kumar wrote to the Director General of IT and senior officers that the statutory functions of registration officers, district election officers and Chief Electoral Officers were to be exercised by them and no one else, and that IT systems must comply with the law.
events.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity

events.title: The software must not limit the ERO
events.text: With the revision under way in 12 states and union territories, Sanjay Kumar asked the Director General of IT to make sure the system did not restrict a registration officer’s discretion.
events.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity

events.title: ECINet launched
events.text: The Commission launched ECINet, bringing more than 40 of its apps and portals, the roll software among them, onto one platform.
events.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity

events.title: Flagged electors to be heard
events.text: The Supreme Court ordered that electors flagged for logical discrepancies be listed in public with the reason, and given ten days to submit documents or objections and be heard before the final roll.
events.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out

events.title: Goa asks for a way to reverse decisions
events.text: Goa’s registration officers had heard 649 flagged electors and found 97 eligible, but ECINet had no way to reverse their earlier entries. Goa’s Chief Electoral Officer forwarded the state software agency’s complaint to the Senior Deputy Election Commissioner in charge of Goa, copied to the Director General of IT.
events.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out

events.title: Goa writes again
events.text: The Chief Electoral Officer’s office wrote that no reply had come, and that 97 cases needed the rollback option.
events.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out

events.title: Two emails and a letter
events.text: Two more emails and a formal letter from the Chief Electoral Officer, Sanjay Goel, saying no response had been received.
events.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out

events.title: “Most urgent”
events.text: Goa wrote that the rollback option was urgently needed to comply with the Supreme Court’s order.
events.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out

events.title: Still no reply
events.text: Goa wrote that a response to every one of its emails and letters was still awaited.
events.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out

events.title: The list of 97
events.text: The eighth message in seven days attached the 97 electors and asked that they be included in the final roll.
events.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out

events.title: “IT system cannot block”
events.text: Sanjay Kumar wrote to the Director General of IT that the system could not block action the Supreme Court had directed, and asked her to let Goa publish the roll as its officers had decided.
events.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out

events.title: Goa’s final roll, without the 97
events.text: Goa published its final roll. The paper checked all 97 names against it and found every one missing as late as 20 September.
events.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out

events.title: Sandhu on decisions taken without the Commission
events.text: Sandhu recorded that communications were going out in the Commission’s name without its approval, and that the IT division had built new modules and portals that were never put to him or to the Commission.
events.headline: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps

events.title: Joshi says the same
events.text: Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi told the same officers that communications were being issued in the Commission’s name without its approval.
events.headline: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps

events.title: Joshi says Form 6 is fixed by law
events.text: Joshi recorded that Form 6 is set by the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and cannot be changed without the government amending them, and advised sending the proposal to the government.
events.headline: ‘Illegal, unauthorised’: Election Commissioners objected to Form 6 change

events.title: Sandhu agrees
events.text: Sandhu concurred with Joshi’s note on Form 6.
events.headline: ‘Illegal, unauthorised’: Election Commissioners objected to Form 6 change

events.title: Joshi asks for an audit
events.text: Joshi wrote of the “gradual centralisation of the electoral roll database” and proposed an audit, with an outside expert from an IIT, to certify that only the statutory officers could change it.
events.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity

events.title: The Form 6 change is reported
events.text: The Indian Express reported that the online Form 6 now asked new applicants whether they, their parents or their grandparents were on the roll of the last intensive revision, and would not let them submit without an answer.
events.headline: EC changes Form 6 for new voters without amendment to rules; seeks SIR details of parents

events.title: Sandhu backs the audit
events.text: Sandhu endorsed Joshi’s audit proposal and asked that it go before the Commission.
events.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity

events.title: Oversight of the IT division removed
events.text: Within hours of taking temporary charge of administration, Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg changed the allocation of work, removing Sanjay Kumar’s oversight of the Director General of IT, without consulting the Commission.
events.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity

events.title: Both write to the Cabinet Secretary
events.text: Sandhu and Joshi each wrote to the Cabinet Secretary, calling the order a clear violation of the 2023 Act and asking for action against the officer.
events.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity

events.title: The order is set aside
events.text: The two Commissioners jointly set the new allocation aside until the Commission agreed on any change.
events.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity

events.title: Sandhu calls the Form 6 change illegal
events.text: Sandhu wrote that the change to the online Form 6 was “unauthorised/illegal” and must be removed at once so that eligible first-time voters could register without harassment.
events.headline: ‘Illegal, unauthorised’: Election Commissioners objected to Form 6 change

events.title: Sandhu says officers are shut out of the roll
events.text: Sandhu recorded that Chief Electoral Officers, district officers and registration officers had told him they lacked proper and complete access to ERONet, that the Director General of IT had no legal authority to restrict them, and that he knew of no action on the audit notes.
events.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity

events.title: The full Commission meets
events.text: The Chief Election Commissioner and the two Commissioners met, their first full meeting in four months.
events.headline: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps

events.title: The investigation is published
events.text: The Indian Express published its account of at least 14 objections in 10 months, after sending the Commission a questionnaire on 21 September that went unanswered.
events.headline: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps

events.title: The Commission replies
events.text: In its press note 119, the Commission said written notes and internal checks were standard practice, that the Commissioners’ suggestions were meant to improve the process, that every decision of the past year had been unanimous, and that ECINet runs under strict security protocols. The Indian Express reported that the note did not answer the specific concerns.
events.headline: Press note ECI/PN/119/2026, 23.09.2026

events.title: The Goa account is published
events.text: The Indian Express published the eight messages from Goa and the 97 electors left off its final roll.
events.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out

events.title: Nine decisions
events.text: After its meeting, the Commission’s press note 120 listed nine decisions. Documents to be collected at home from those sent notices, help desks and camps for the homeless and the poor, the statutory Form 6 outside the revision, a review of ECINet by a committee with an IIT or IIIT expert and new IT modules to go through a committee of officers, later dates in Delhi and Maharashtra, agendas and minutes for every meeting, appraisal reports on time, the Commission’s approval for officers’ foreign trips, and Commissioners’ directions to be complied with. It ordered a special drive to enrol those left out, said the letter to the Cabinet Secretary concerned an officer on deputation whose reallocation of work was never put into effect, and said 81 of Goa’s 97 had filled in Form 6.
events.headline: Press note ECI/PN/120/2026, 26.09.2026

events.title: A drive for those left out
events.text: A letter from the Commission’s Secretary told the 20 states and union territories where the revision is over to run a special drive to enrol left-out and first-time electors, on the statutory Form 6, and kept the declaration for the revision period only.
events.headline: After 13 crore names dropped from draft rolls, EC orders ‘left out’ voter drive

events.title: “Not approved by us”
events.text: Hearing a petition against decisions said to have been taken by the Chief Election Commissioner alone, the Chief Justice observed that no modified Form 6 had been approved by the Supreme Court.
events.headline: CJI Surya Kant: Any modification to Form 6 not approved by Supreme Court

inside.note: The Indian Express says it has seen these notes and letters. This site has not, and none is public. Every entry below is the paper’s account, linked to its article, except the Commission’s own press notes of 23 and 26 September, which link to the notes.
inside.issue: The paper collected the series in a special issue of its Express Plus magazine, "Election Commission of India: lapses and challenges", in October 2026, and released it free.
